verdict.rationale: Lambda's docs explicitly state ODC 'prices instances by hourly usage and bills in one-minute increments' (docs-10), satisfying per-minute granularity while running, and usage can be tracked on a per-instance basis (docs-20). However, billing is only per-minute (not per-second), and a community report shows a user billed for 391 hours because Lambda 'does not distinguish between idle and in use instance states'—meaning the meter keeps running whenever the instance is up, with no auto-stop protection, which undercuts the practical 'only while running=only while useful' expectation. missing for 10: per-second granularity, independent confirmation of billing accuracy, and auto-stop/idle-detection to prevent unexpected charges.
